subject: Retailer addendum — pass-through invoicing & credits (invoice routing handshake)
messages:
From: Irene Shaw <irene.shaw@cloudretailer.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Cc: Cloud Retailer Finance <ap.payments@cloudretailer.com>
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Retailer addendum — pass-through invoicing & credits

Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking this. Quick background: Cloud Retailer is preparing to onboard Redwood into our marketplace and legal asked us to surface one item before we sign — the pass-through invoicing and credit flow for marketplace fees and any downstream refunds/chargebacks. We've attached our standard addendum (CR_Addendum_v1.docx) and a one-page flow diagram (CR_invoice-flow-diagram.png).

High level asks from finance and procurement:
- We need a clean description of how marketplace fees are invoiced to Cloud Retailer and whether Redwood will issue credit notes back to the marketplace or to our merchants.
- If Redwood collects marketplace fees on behalf of third-party sellers, what evidence will be provided to support pass-through amounts?
- Does Redwood require an escrow or holdback, or can fees be netted on a consolidated monthly invoice?
- Expected payment terms: our finance team prefers net30. Can Redwood confirm?

Can you (and legal) review and share any redlines or a short proposal of the invoice routing we can present to our CPO and procurement this week? If it helps, we can do a 30-minute call Tuesday morning PT.

Thanks,
Irene Shaw
Head of Marketplace Partnerships
Cloud Retailer
Mobile: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: CR_Addendum_v1.docx (draft addendum, 6 pages); CR_invoice-flow-diagram.png (1 page)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Irene Shaw <irene.shaw@cloudretailer.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 31 Jul 2027 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retailer addendum — pass-through invoicing & credits

Thanks Irene — appreciate the clear summary and the diagram.

Quick reply while I loop in legal and ops: we can support two practical models depending on your operational preference:

Option A (Consolidated monthly invoice): Redwood issues a single monthly invoice to Cloud Retailer that nets marketplace fees and includes an itemized schedule for pass-through components. We can support net30. This is operationally simplest and avoids escrow.

Option B (Marketplace-collected / invoiced to merchants): Redwood routes fees through the marketplace and provides a monthly reconciliation package and credit notes for any refunds/chargebacks. This requires sample evidence (transaction-level CSV + settlement report) and a 30-day window for any adjustments.

Legal caveat: we typically avoid open-ended escrow obligations or unlimited audit-triggered holdbacks. I'll let Neha propose contract language, but operationally the consolidated monthly invoice (Option A) is our recommended default.

Would you be available for a short call Tuesday 08/02 at 10:00am PT to align finance and contract language? I'm attaching a light redline with our preferred language (GRACE_redlines_v1.docx) for your team to review before the call.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: GRACE_redlines_v1.docx (inline-comments: invoicing model + pass-through cap)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Irene Shaw <irene.shaw@cloudretailer.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retailer addendum — pass-through invoicing & credits

On Sat, Jul 31, 2027 at 9:12 AM Irene Shaw <irene.shaw@cloudretailer.com> wrote:
> Hi Grace,
> 
> Thanks for taking this. Quick background...

Irene / Grace — copying a short legal note and proposed redline below so procurement has language to review. Grace's Option A is acceptable from a risk standpoint with the following guardrails we would like in the addendum: 

1) Pass-through cap: Redwood will not be liable for amounts greater than the fees actually invoiced to the marketplace; we will pass through amounts that are substantiated by transaction-level records.
2) Audit scope: Cloud Retailer may request transactional evidence no more than once per 12 months and limited to a single prior 12-month period (unless there's a good faith suspicion of fraud). Redwood will provide a summarized CSV and settlement report rather than raw card data.
3) Credit notes: If a downstream refund/chargeback occurs, Redwood will issue a credit to Cloud Retailer on the next monthly invoice, and any upstream adjustment deadlines are limited to 90 days from the transaction date.
4) Payment terms: Redwood can accept net30 for the consolidated invoice but requests a clause allowing recovery of collection costs for past-due amounts over 60 days.

Proposed contract snippet (redline-ready):
"Redwood shall issue a consolidated monthly invoice to Customer that itemizes pass-through marketplace fees. Customer may request transaction-level supporting documentation no more than once per twelve (12) month period for the twelve (12) month period immediately preceding the request. Redwood's liability for pass-through fees shall be limited to amounts actually invoiced and substantiated by Redwood's reconciliation reports. Credit notes for refunds or chargebacks will be applied to the following monthly invoice if the underlying transaction is reported to Redwood within ninety (90) days of the transaction date."

Please advise if Cloud Retailer needs a different audit cadence or has regulatory constraints requiring more frequent evidence. If not, we can lock language and I will prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum once we get a green light from your procurement.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: excerpted redline will be shared in DocuSign package once terms are agreed)

From: Irene Shaw <irene.shaw@cloudretailer.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: Cloud Retailer Finance <ap.payments@cloudretailer.com>, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 2 Aug 2027 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Retailer addendum — pass-through invoicing & credits

Grace/Neha — thanks for the quick turn. The language Neha proposed looks reasonable to our procurement and finance teams. Two small asks before we finalize:

1) Can Redwood confirm the monthly reconciliation CSV will include (a) date/time, (b) marketplace ID, (c) gross fee, (d) fee type (platform/transaction), and (e) a settlement reference? Our ops team needs that to automate postings.
2) Can you cap the audit request to "one annual review with 30 days' notice" (we prefer 30 days notice vs immediate requests) — if that wording is acceptable we can route to our CPO for signature.

If you confirm these two items, I'll ask procurement to approve the addendum and we'll sign via DocuSign. After signature Finance will expect the first consolidated invoice at the close of the next month.

If it helps, we can take the DocuSign envelope and a short statement of work for the onboarding date on the same day.

Thanks,
Irene

Attachments: (none new)
